subject: ORD function
notes: OVERTURNED from CONFORMS. HOLDS on the identity PCS (Ord(s) = s[0]+1, lowest ordinal 1 per §15.70.1 — IF127A pins ORD("5")=54) and on a non-identity alphabet that lists only Latin-1 characters with no ALSO (ca26 pins ORD=00257). FAILS on two other paths, both reproduced with the built CLI at --std 2023. (1) The ALSO path is wrong INSIDE the ORD runtime itself: CobolIntrinsics.Text.Ord(string, ushort[] weights) returns 'c + 1L' for any code unit at or beyond the 256-entry table, but an ALSO group collapses positions so the tail no longer coincides with the native ordinal. Program: OBJECT-COMPUTER PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE AL / SPECIAL-NAMES ALPHABET AL IS "A" ALSO "B" / 01 W PIC X VALUE <U+0100> — ORD(X"FF") printed 00255 (position 254, the top of Latin-1) and ORD(W) printed 00257, i.e. position 256, SKIPPING position 255; §12.3.7 GR7 k3 gives unspecified characters DISTINCT ASCENDING positions with no gap, so U+0100 sits at position 255 and r1's returned value is 256. The correct arithmetic already exists on the national twin — NationalCollation.Weight uses NextFree + (c − |specified codes below c|) and the same ALSO probe on ALPHABET RN FOR NATIONAL IS N"A" ALSO N"B" printed the right ORD(N"C")=00067. (2) AlphabetBind's position table is a fixed ushort[256] built with 'int code = c & 0xFF', but the alphanumeric repertoire is UTF-16 (the compiler's own established design, asserted in ca26's header), so an ALPHABET literal character above U+00FF is silently aliased to its low byte and never gets its declared position. Program: ALPHABET AL IS "<U+0100>" with PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE AL printed ORD(U+0100)=00257, ORD(X"00")=00001, ORD("A")=00066; §12.3.7 GR7 k1b/k3 give 1, 2 and 67 — every character in the program reports the wrong ordinal position, so r1's 'the returned value is the ordinal position of argument-1 in the current alphanumeric program collating sequence' is false throughout. The prior verdict deflected (2) to §12.3.7 on the grounds that 'ORD faithfully reports whatever the table holds': that is not true, because for c >= 256 ORD never consults the table at all, and even a correctly built table would not repair defect (1). FIX SHAPE: widen CollatingTable.Positions off the Latin-1 assumption (or give the alphanumeric side the same sparse NextFree arithmetic the national side already has) and delete the 'c + 1L' shortcut. Existing tests do not cover either path — an ALSO alphabet plus an above-Latin-1 ORD golden is test-needed.

subject: ORD function

subject: ORD-MAX function
notes: Downgraded from CONFORMS. What HOLDS, read and re-verified by running: the alphanumeric leg does §8.8.4.2.7 rule 2 space-padding (CobolString.Compare extends the shorter operand to Math.Max length with the pad; ORD-MAX("A" "A ") -> 1) and weighs through the alphanumeric program collating sequence (the ushort[] overload via CollatePrefix) — under `OBJECT-COMPUTER. XX PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS REV. ALPHABET REV IS "Z" "Y" "X" "A" "B" "C"`, ORD-MAX("A" "Z") returned 1 and the program's own `IF S1 > S2` printed A-GT-Z, i.e. the function agrees with the relation condition; the national leg goes through the NationalCollation overload per §8.8.4.2.9; and the fixed-point numeric leg aligns every argument to the common scale (widening only, exact) so the unscaled Int128 compare IS the §8.8.4.2.4 algebraic comparison. What does NOT hold: (a) §8.8.4.2.4 makes a floating-point operand class numeric and requires the algebraic comparison, but for a COMP-1/COMP-2 argument NO comparison is generated at all — the call fails to compile (CS1503, the AlignedArgs/AnyReal defect recorded under RV-15.71.4-1); recording it here too because a CONFORMS row is never revisited and this rule is not satisfied for that operand shape. (b) §8.8.4.2.4 paragraph 3 requires, under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY, that the comparison be performed as if each operand were converted to a standard-binary intermediate data item under the INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING mode; the renderer's `OrdMax or OrdMin` case has no arithmetic-mode branch and BindIntrinsicCore's §15.4.1 loud-staging list is only ANNUITY/PRESENT-VALUE/VARIANCE/STANDARD-DEVIATION and does not even test ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary, so the exact Int128 comparison is used silently in that mode. Test coverage: nist:IF128A tests 07/08 are genuine unequal-length alphanumeric comparisons (ORD-MAX("A", I, "P") with I PIC X(4) VALUE "R"), but the collating-sequence leg is UNCOVERED for ORD-MAX — tests/conformance/2002/intrinsic_max_collating.cob names ORD-MAX only in its comment and calls FUNCTION MAX alone. test-needed: a PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE case calling ORD-MAX, and a floating-point-argument case.

subject: ORD-MAX function
notes: Both selection bodies were read: OrdMax does `if (xs[i] > m)` and ExtremeIndex does `if (max ? c > 0 : c < 0)` — a STRICTLY-greater update, so an argument equal to the running maximum never displaces it and the leftmost position is returned. subject: PI function
notes: CobolIntrinsics.Pi() = Math.PI is a legitimate implementor-defined approximation of (3 + 0.1415926535897932384626433832795), and the documentation obligation is discharged: Annex A.1 item 92 (validated - 'Function returned values (characteristics, representation, and returned value for native arithmetic) ... The value returned does not have to be documented') exempts the VALUE while still requiring the characteristics/representation, and those ARE documented in CONFORMANCE.md SS7 (the row keyed '- (SS15.4.1 / SS14.9.11.4 GR1)', read and confirmed to state that a FLOAT-valued function renders through the same shortest-round-trip CobolFloat.Display a COMP-2 item does). PARTIAL for a receiver-shape leg, re-verified independently on the built CLI at --std 2023: IntrinsicRenderer.RenderFloat quantizes through the ONE FromDouble at ws = max(Receiver.Scale, 9), and FromDouble's scaled double exceeds Int64 at scale >= 19 and SATURATES to long.MaxValue with no size error and no diagnostic - '01 R19 PIC 9V9(19). COMPUTE R19 = FUNCTION PI. DISPLAY R19.' prints 0.9223372036854775807 and PIC 9V9(30) prints 0.000000000009223372036854775807. Neither is an approximation of pi, so rule 1 is violated for every legal 2002+ receiver of 20..31 digits (scale <= 18 is fine: PIC 9V9(18) prints 3.141592653589793280, within approximation license). Not PI-specific - the whole SS15.4.1 float family funnels through the same FromDouble. TEST COVERAGE: the cited test does compile-and-run and asserts the value 3.14159, so it genuinely covers rule 1's happy path, but only at PIC 9.9(5) and only at edition 2014 (AssertSpec dialect argument); the scale >= 19 saturation leg and editions 2002/2023 are test-needed.

subject: PI function
notes: EDITIONS CORRECTED to 2014,2023: standard-decimal arithmetic is a COBOL-2014 introduction (ConstructRegistry row 'arithmetic-standard-decimal-2014', IntroducedIn 2014) - re-verified, 'OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL.' at --std 2002 is rejected with COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2014 (targeting COBOL-2002)'. SS15.73.3 rule 3 requires the returned value to be EXACTLY 3.141592653589793238462643383279503; PI is absent from the IntrinsicBinder staged-loud list (which holds only ANNUITY / PRESENT-VALUE / VARIANCE / STANDARD-DEVIATION) and rides the ordinary RenderFloat/Math.PI/binary64 path in EVERY arithmetic mode, so a STANDARD-DECIMAL program silently gets native binary64 digits. FAILING INPUT (re-run independently on the built CLI): 'IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. PROGRAM-ID. PISDREV2. OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL. DATA DIVISION. WORKING-STORAGE SECTION. 01 R17 PIC 9V9(17). PROCEDURE DIVISION. COMPUTE R17 = FUNCTION PI. DISPLAY R17.' at --std 2014 and --std 2023 prints 3.14159265358979328; rule 3 truncated to the receiver (COMPUTE without ROUNDED truncates, SS14.7) requires 3.14159265358979323 - note the earlier draft's expected '...324' was the ROUNDED value and is wrong. At PIC 9V9(30) it prints 0.000000000009223372036854775807 (the FromDouble Int64 saturation) against a required 3.141592653589793238462643383279. THE FALSE PREMISE, written in two places - the CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs class header and the IntrinsicBinder staging comment - is 'their returned-value rules are prose approximations, NOT equivalent arithmetic expressions, so the value is implementor-defined in EVERY mode (SS15.4.1 last paragraph)'. It fails on TWO independent grounds, both validated: (a) SS15.73.3 rule 1 is phrased exactly as SS15.4.1's equivalent-arithmetic-expression sentence ('an implementor-defined approximation of the arithmetic expression (3 + 0.14159...)'), so PI DOES have an EAE, and SS15.4.1 then states 'When standard-decimal arithmetic or standard-binary arithmetic is in effect and an equivalent arithmetic expression is specified: 1) the returned value shall equal the value of the equivalent arithmetic expression'; and (b) even on the no-EAE reading, SS15.4.1's last paragraph reads 'its returned value is implementor-defined UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN THE FUNCTION DEFINITION' - and rules 2 and 3 are precisely that specification. Test-needed (no test references PI under any standard arithmetic mode). SIBLING CONFIRMED, not merely suspected: 'COMPUTE R17 = FUNCTION E.' under STANDARD-DECIMAL prints 2.71828182845904512 where SS15.27.3 rule 3 (validated) requires the exact value truncating to 2.71828182845904523. ALSO: ArithmeticMode.Standard (the 2002-2014 'ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD' clause, which DataBinder routes to the same CobolDec engine) diverges identically - verified, --std 2002 with ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD prints the same 3.14159265358979328 - so the fix must cover ArithmeticMode.Standard as well as StandardDecimal.

subject: PRESENT-VALUE function
notes: test-needed. §15.74.3 r2 (cite.py --check: OK) — the value of argument-1 shall be greater than −1. This is a permissible-VALUE constraint, so §15.3 applies: 'If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument … the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist'; Annex A.1 item 90 makes only the RETURNED VALUE implementor-defined when checking is off — the condition must still be SET, and must be raised when checking is on. CobolIntrinsics.PresentValue(double rate, params double[] amounts) performs no domain check on rate, unlike its file-mates Log/Log10 which call Exceptions.ExceptionState.ArgumentError, and the binder adds none. Reproduced with the built CLI: (a) COMPILE-TIME-detectable literal violation, edition-independent — `COMPUTE RESULT-X = FUNCTION PRESENT-VALUE(-1.5, 100, 200)` is accepted silently at --std 85 AND --std 2023 and prints 600.000000, so the divergence does not depend on the (2002+) EC machinery and holds at every edition; (b) runtime rate with checking explicitly enabled — `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON` then `FUNCTION PRESENT-VALUE(R2 AMT AMT)` with R2 = −2.00 prints 0 and CONTINUES, while the very next `FUNCTION LOG(0)` in the SAME program aborts with 'EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal)' — same directive, same run unit, so the mechanism exists and PRESENT-VALUE alone does not use it; (c) rate = −1.00 exactly makes 1+rate = 0, and the binary64 division through FromDouble SATURATES, printing 223372036.8547 with no exception and no diagnostic.

subject: PRESENT-VALUE function
notes: Holds under NATIVE arithmetic; the standard-arithmetic leg does not. The body `for (int i = 0; i < amounts.Length; i++) pv += amounts[i] / Math.Pow(1 + rate, i + 1)` is exactly Σ argument-2ᵢ / (1 + argument-1)^i for i = 1..n — §15.74.4 r1c, with r1a and r1b as its n = 1 and n = 2 cases — and §15.4.1 licenses 'an implementor-defined approximation' under native arithmetic. Verified with the built CLI: PRESENT-VALUE(0.100 1000 2000 3000) and the hand-written FUNCTION SUM EAE both give 4815.927873, which is also the exact hand-computed value. Annex A.1 item 92 ('Function returned values (characteristics, representation, and returned value for native arithmetic) … The value returned does not have to be documented') means the documentation test does NOT downgrade the native leg, and docs/CONFORMANCE.md already carries a §15.4.1 / §14.9.11.4 GR1 row. THE PARTIAL: §15.4.1 r1 requires the returned value to EQUAL the equivalent arithmetic expression when standard-decimal OR STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic is in effect, and instead of doing so IntrinsicBinder rejects the program with DiagnosticCatalog.ArithmeticStandardIntrinsic (COBOLNET0899, EditionSeverity.Error) — legal COBOL refused; confirmed by running an OPTIONS/ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL program. ⚠ NOTE FOR THE FIX SESSION: that staging condition is `ctx.Data.Options.Arithmetic is ArithmeticMode.Standard or ArithmeticMode.StandardDecimal` and OMITS ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary, which §15.4.1 covers equally. I checked whether that opens a SILENT-wrong-answer hole and it does not — today ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is itself loud-rejected earlier by COBOLNET0806 ('obsolete feature … not supported') at --std 85/2002/2014/2023, so standard-binary can never be in effect — but if 0806 is ever lifted (obsolete is not removed; §11.9.5 still defines the phrase in 2023), the 0899 list must gain StandardBinary or PRESENT-VALUE will silently return the native double. The rule itself applies at all four editions; the failing leg needs the OPTIONS ARITHMETIC clause and so is reachable only from 2002. ⚠ TEST-REF CORRECTED: nist:IF403M was STRUCK on two independent grounds — it is registered 'pending / none / cataloged (not asserted)' in tests/nist/corpus.tsv line 406 so nothing runs it, and its sole PRESENT-VALUE statement compares the function to ITSELF (`IF FUNCTION PRESENT-VALUE (0, 23, 12, 9) = FUNCTION PRESENT-VALUE (0, 23, 12, 9)`), which tests determinism, never the equivalent arithmetic expression. nist:IF130A genuinely covers the native leg — F-PRES-VAL-01 range-checks PRESENT-VALUE(0, 23, 12, 9) against 43.9991..44.0009 and twenty-one further paragraphs range-check real values. subject: RANDOM function
notes: Neither half of 'it shall be zero or a positive integer' is enforced at bind or at run time, and the §15.3 raise ('If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument ... the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist') never fires for a RANDOM seed. subject: RANDOM function
notes: The runtime body conforms (Random.NextDouble() is in [0,1)) and the FLOAT-receiver path (num.Receiver.Real) hands the double through unquantized. The FIXED-POINT receiver path does NOT: RenderFloat wraps the call in FromDouble(call, ws) with ws = Math.Max(num.Receiver.Scale, 9), and FromDouble ends in `(long)Math.Round(scaled, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero)`, so any returned value >= 0.9999999995 quantizes to exactly 1.000000000 — not 'less than one'. THE QUANTIZATION DEFECT IS DEMONSTRATED, not conjectured: on the same shared code path `01 R PIC 9V9(9). COMPUTE R = FUNCTION SQRT(0.999999999).` prints 1.000000000 while SQRT(0.999999998) prints 0.999999999. For RANDOM the top bucket is one draw in ~2.1e9 (the seeded back-compat generator's NextDouble is InternalSample() * (1.0/int.MaxValue) and only InternalSample() == 2147483646 clears the threshold; the argument-less xoshiro path has the same ~5e-10 probability), so no short deterministic COBOL input exhibits it — the bound is broken by the emitter's generic rounding, not by the generator. The prior adjudication argued this away as 'always resolves to EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION', but §15.3's EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION disposition is for an argument whose evaluation produces an INCORRECT VALUE; r1 is a static class rule, and this compiler's own precedent for a §15 argument class rule is a BIND-time diagnostic (CheckRepertoireArgs → COBOLNET1546 for DISPLAY-OF/NATIONAL-OF §15.26.3/§15.66.3). subject: SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: §15.79.3 r2 requires argument-1's CONTENT to be a time format (§15.3.2/§15.3.3) or a combined date and time format (§15.3.3.7), but nothing anywhere checks the format's KIND or its well-formedness beyond tokenizability: Tokenize only returns null for an unknown character or a bad field-character run, and neither the binder nor CobolDate asks whether an hours/minutes/seconds subfield is present. Four verified holes, all compiling clean and returning a value with no diagnostic and no EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION even under `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON`: (1) a DATE-only format — `FUNCTION SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME("YYYYMMDD", "20210616")` → +000000000; (2) a partial time that is no format at all — `("hhmm", "1234")` → +000045240, though §15.3.3.1 makes hh, mm AND ss all mandatory in a common time format; (3) an illegal basic/extended MIXTURE — `("YYYY-MM-DDThhmmss", "2021-06-16T123456")` → +45296.00, which §15.3.3.7 expressly forbids ('Combinations of basic date formats with extended time formats, or of extended date formats with basic time formats, are not allowed'); (4) a fraction wider than any defined maximum — `("hhmmss.ssssssssss", …)` is accepted although §15.3.3.2 makes the maximum implementor-defined (floor nine) and COBOL.NET defines none (see RV-15.79.4-1). subject: SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: ((H*3600)+(M*60)+S) is computed exactly for fraction widths up to NINE digits — Analyze forms `((long)hh*3600 + mi*60 + ss) * 10^f + frac` at scale f, S correctly carrying the fractional-second digits of the seconds subfield (§15.3.3.2), and the offset/UTC subfields correctly NOT entering the sum; both D.31.5.9 worked examples reproduce exactly ("hhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"05142781+0500" and "YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"19950215T05142781+0500" → +18867.81). Verified at --std 2014: `("hhmmss.ssssssssss", "1234563000000000")` into `01 WS-A PIC +9(5).9(10).` returns +45295.8705032704 instead of +45296.3000000000 (3000000000 − 2^32 = −1294967296); twelve digits `("hhmmss.ssssssssssss", "123456812479168304")` into PIC +9(5).9(12) returns +45296.000730349360 instead of +45296.812479168304; nineteen digits returns +00000.01. §15.3.3.2 makes the maximum fraction width implementor-defined with a floor of nine; COBOL.NET neither enforces nor documents a maximum, and A.1 item 202 ('Time formats and corresponding function values (maximum precision not less than nine fractional digits)', required, 'This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation') is documented in CONFORMANCE.md §7: NO — §7 currently lists only items 2, 59, 158 and 205–215. So the conforming fix is BOTH halves: widen the accumulator (or reject past the defined maximum with EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION) AND add the item-202 row to CONFORMANCE.md §7. The two existing tests exercise the expression only at 0 and 2 fraction digits, so nothing covers the overflow.

CONCRETE RISK: cobol --std 2002 today rejects FUNCTION ABS with COBOLNET1502 'was introduced by ISO/IEC 1989:2014', so if ABS is in fact a 2002 function the compiler rejects legal COBOL-2002.
